summary: This memo discusses problems that arise, and debugging techniques used, when bringing a new network into operation. It is written in a light-hearted style.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 968 is a poem about a network that does not work on the night before startup. An experienced engineer checks the system, but the narrator's final explanation is an off-by-one index error.

subtitle: A poem about troubleshooting a network that fails on startup.

tldr.problem: A new network can fail to move packets even when its components and protocols appear to be in place.
tldr.mechanism: The poem describes an experienced engineer checking alarms, protocols, and a suspect line before the narrator discovers an off-by-one index error.
tldr.outcome: The memo presents network startup and troubleshooting as a humorous poem, ending with a simple indexing mistake.

today: RFC 968 is a poem discussing problems and debugging techniques in bringing a network into operation. Its text ends with the narrator finding an off-by-one index error.

sections.title: The Failed Network Startup
sections.content:
The poem begins on the night before startup, when no packet is moving and the engineers are worried. The narrator has diagnostic traces and dumps ready while expecting a difficult failure.

An experienced ARPANET hacker arrives and begins checking alarms and network components.
sections.plainLanguage: The network is due to start, but packets are not moving. The poem describes the engineers' concern before a troubleshooter begins work.

sections.title: Systematic Troubleshooting
sections.content:
The poem lists LAPB, OSI, X.25, TCP, SNA, and V.35 as the troubleshooter checks the system. It describes a patch to a suspect line, after which the network comes up and packets flow.

The poem then says the protocols matched, hosts interfaced, shift registers latched, and the tests from gateway to PAD passed.
sections.plainLanguage: The troubleshooter checks components and protocols in turn, finds a suspect line, and applies a patch. The poem reports that the network then passes its checks.

sections.title: The Off-by-One Ending
sections.content:
After the network appears to work, the narrator asks why the system had died. The poem ends by saying an off-by-one index in the narrator's code had caused the problem again.

The conclusion turns the apparent network-wide crisis into a counting error in the narrator's own code.
sections.plainLanguage: The final cause is an off-by-one index in the narrator's code. The poem ends by making the simple mistake the punch line.
